recipes.name: Chinese Pepper Steak
ingredients_raw: 1 green bell pepper, cut into 1-inch squares

steps.text: Slice steak into 1/2-inch-thick slices across the grain and place into a large bowl.
Whisk soy sauce, sugar, cornstarch, and ginger in a small bowl until sugar is dissolved and marinade is smooth. Pour marinade over steak and stir until well coated.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat. Working in batches, cook and stir steak in hot oil until well browned, about 3 minutes. Remove steak to a plate. Repeat with remaining steak, adding more oil as needed.
Return cooked steak strips to the hot wok; stir in onion. Toss steak and onion together until onion begins to soften, about 2 minutes, then stir in green pepper.
Cook and stir until peppers turn bright green and start to become tender, about 2 minutes more, then add tomatoes.
Stir until well combined and the flavors are blended.

raw_recipe.headline: Chinese Pepper Steak
raw_recipe.description: This easy and delicious pepper steak recipe combines top sirloin beef with a sweet-and-savory soy sauce marinade, green pepper, onion, and tomatoes.

video.description: Watch how to take a piece of steak and turn it into a sweet-and-savory stir fry dish with vegetables. The secret is to cut the steak against the grain and quickly marinate it in soy sauce with sugar, cornstarch and ginger. Stir in the vegetables, and dinner is ready in just half an hour.

review.reviewBody:
This is great the way it is. I wish people would review the recipe not add there own sweet and sour version of it. Add a new recipe with your sweet and sour version. I think it inappropriate to add in the comments.
Thanks for your original recipe Mrs Wilson.

Made it without marinading...just threw everything together after browning the steak strips in the oil. I doubled all the other ingredients and completely forgot to add the tomatoes. (the main reason I chose this recipe) Still Delicious! Oh, I did use fresh ginger that I was trying to use up instead of ground.

My whole family loves this (and anyone else who'se dined at our house when it's served) I make up the "marinade" a day ahead, sometimes two. We like a lot of sauce so I triple the amount of marinade. I use avocado oil in my pan (or wok) and I try to drain the marinade as much as possible from the meat because the marinade has sugar in it, it tends to carmelize onto the sides of the pan. When I add the veggies I keep it covered, then after I add the tomatoes, I add all of the reserved marinade to the pan and lower the temp a bit and cover it and let it simmer. I try to buy choice sirloin but I think if you let it marinade overnight, it tends to be more tender.

Solid good recipe! My only change was in step 4; which asks me add the steak - which has already been cooked - again. I didn’t want my steak over cooked but I also wanted my onions and peppers to be tender crisp. As such, I gave the onion/peppers a head start - sautéd for about 5 min, and then added the sirloin and tomatoes as asked in step 5. Tomatoes were easy to pick out if you didn’t like but I did! This is easy to make and satisfies that Chinese take out craving!! Would and will make again! Thanks Kim!!

This is a GREAT base recipe, and the cooking times were exactly right, but imo, it needed a little more color and flavor. So the 2nd time I made it, I used half green and half red pepper. At the end, I added about a TBSP Worcerstershire Sauce and liberally sprinkled it with Montreal Steak Seasoning (2 passes over the pan or wok), an extra pass of soy sauce, and a pinch of red pepper flakes. I like the other suggestions of maybe a minced garlic clove or two also. I LOVED the fresh tomato wedges thrown in at the end! It's a nice looking dish and it all goes together in less than an hour easily! Great basic recipe to make your way but start here! It's great the way it is for a family with small children, but you might want to double the recipe for 4. Thx! I'll keep this one handy! Served over Basmati white rice simmered - covered tightly in beef broth for 20 min.

Made it using low sodium soy sauce, and after the tomatoes I put a dash of white pepper. I believe it’s all in the meat, I let it sit in the brine for a bit for more flavor before putting in wok. Don’t overcook the veggies, cooked but crunchy. Loved the flavor👍
I double the marinade because we like it and poured the remainder of it in the pan and let it cook for 5 more minutes... Yummy!!

Terrific! I have a penchant for real ginger, so I shredded half cubic inch of raw root, tossing that in on the onion stage "fry" (sauté). No hurt to the dish for us ginger people. Also now, 5th time I have made this, added 1/2 tsp of pepper flakes to give it even more oomph. I also used very thin cooked steak. Marinaded, nonetheless. Throwing that in with the ginger/onion stage to great effect.

I am an Asian food junkie and I loved this recipe. I did use fresh ginger and local honey instead of sugar. My main change was that I cooked the beef for about 6 minutes at fairly high temp and removed it to a covered dish. I then cooked all the vegetables in order of slowest cooking to fastest in the pan juices then re-added the beef and stirred until warmed through and well combined.

This is a wonderful recipe. Just a little hint - if the steak is partially frozen - your cuts will be more precise and the meat won't wiggle as much! Plus I added a little pinch of red pepper flakes YUMMY Lisa Barnett

I made tis in the crockpot because I used round steak. I browned it after cutting into strips. I used salt free Chinese 5 spice instead of the ginger. I dumped in a bag of frozen peppers and onions, and about 20 cherry tomatoes I cut in half. Was delicious.
A great use of fresh peppers. Tomato isn't necessary.
It makes great pepper steak sandwiches

I used a ribeye steak that had been previously seasoned and cooked. It was delicious! Best pepper steak I ever ate. Loved the sweetness. Also used yellow pepper and cherry tomatoes. No need for additional soy sauce. It was perfect.
Great Fresh everything, Quick and easy to follow and make.

The sauce is so good, I doubled it, but did use beef broth for some of the extra soy sauce. Very versatile - can change vegetables up - I may use snow pea pods instead of green pepper, julienned carrots instead of tomatoes and possibly pineapple next time.
Delicious! I add mushrooms and serve over coconut jasmine rice... my family loves it!
Easy and so good! My husband was not too sure when I was making it then he loved!

Delicious and easy. I used a red pepper and added a cup of chopped (leftover) sugar snap peas. We love ginger and I used 2 of the frozen ginger cubes from Trader Joe's. It was wonderful. The tomatoes added a sweetness and complimented the dish nicely. Will definitely make again and probably double it! Thank you for a great recipe!
no changes
